correctness.rationale: For the cited input, the zero-one-count classes are disjoint; the one-one count is a union of nested initial segments and the three-one count is a product of the two minimum gap bounds plus one in each coordinate. With two ones and a≤d, the first two original ones yield a rectangle contained in the rectangle from the outside ones, and the last two contribute exactly min(b,d−a)(c+1) beyond it. Reversal gives the other branch. All gaps may vanish; the formula then gives the three nonempty palindromes in 111. Uniform labeled positions give uniform integer compositions of n−3. Riemann sums in three coordinates after division by n tend to uniform simplex measure; removing all degree-one and constant terms leaves the stated continuous piecewise quadratic with uniform error O(1/n) after scaling. Boundedness gives convergence of both raw moments. For four independent exponential coordinates, the radial sum is independent Gamma(4,1) and the orientation of the two outside gaps is symmetric. Their independent minimum and difference have rates 2 and 1. Independently computing the first two moments of the resulting homogeneous polynomial over the six orderings of the inner two exponentials and the outer difference gives E G=7/4 and E G²=289/36. Dividing by the radial second and fourth moments 20 and 840 gives the stated moments and variance. No independence across n is needed.
correctness.verification: python3 /workspace/reproducibility/frozen_checks.py 1 matches all 3,876 cases through n=18 using a palindrome-only recurrence based on the outermost occurrences of each wrapping letter. Independent rational integration in exponential spacings on all six order sectors gives mean 7/80, raw second moment 289/30240, and variance 2299/1209600. These reproduce the finite domain and exact constants; the general law uses the analytic argument. The supplied script was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Exactly three ones is a natural finite-weight stratum: overlapping two-one embeddings create competing gap rectangles absent in the simplest cases. The exact positive limiting variance shows that the resulting random gap geometry remains visible at quadratic scale, not merely in lower-order fluctuations. The explicit law and numerical moments are useful reference information for sparse-word comparisons beyond the known deterministic count.
